questions.question: For a first DUI conviction, what could happen to you?

options.text: Lose your license for up to five years.
Take a public education class about drunk driving.
Drive with a restricted occupational license.
Pay a fine of at least $300.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay a fine of at least $300.
questions.explanation: A first DUI conviction includes a fine between $300 and $5,000. The exact amount depends on your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Signal the lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use a different route.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase your following distance. Your car will need more time to stop than on dry roads.

questions.question: If you need to stop suddenly when other drivers may not expect it, what should you do?

options.text: Tap your brake pedal a few times quickly.
Use your emergency brake.
Look over your shoulder for traffic.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times quickly.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake suddenly, tap your brake pedal three or four times quickly. This warns other drivers behind you.

questions.question: What is the speed limit when yellow lights flash on a school zone sign?

options.text: 25 mph
15 mph
20 mph
35 mph

questions.explanation: When yellow lights flash on a school zone sign, the speed limit is 15 mph. This applies during school zone hours.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all the tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the first train passes.
Go when one of the tracks is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: At a multi-track crossing, wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Do not move until you are sure no other train is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shift.
Low clearance.
Extra lane ahead.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic is coming from the opposite direction. Be ready for oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign appears at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It means you cannot drive in that direction.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Other drivers' headlights can blind you. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Beating bad drivers by staying ahead of them.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Changing lanes quickly through heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means seeing dangerous situations early and taking action to prevent accidents. It helps you handle aggressive, careless, tired, or impaired drivers and pedestrians safely.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane of a multilane highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal light.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on a layer of water on the road. Low tire pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with its siren and/or lights approaches you, you must:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with its lights or siren, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Should drive slowly so approaching vehicles and pedestrians can move out of your way.
Should honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Must stop and only proceed when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only proceed when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway and yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes and see a bicyclist ahead going the same direction. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass while leaving enough space.
Keep driving straight. The bicyclist should get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait until no traffic is coming, then pass while leaving enough space.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads or 5 feet on high-speed roads. Honking can startle riders and cause them to crash.

questions.question: If you are under 21 and convicted of carrying a false ID card, you will pay a $500 fine and lose your license for 90 days:

options.text: Only if your blood alcohol level is 0.02 percent or higher.
Even if you were not driving.
Only if you were driving at the time of arrest.
Only if your blood alcohol level is 0.02 percent or higher and you were driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if you were not driving.
questions.explanation: If you are under 21 and convicted of carrying a false ID card, your license will be suspended even if you were not driving. The minimum penalty is a $500 fine and a 90-day license suspension.

questions.question: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Does not affect your driving abilities.
Helps keep you alert while driving.
Is a distraction.
Is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction because it takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: When passing a bicyclist, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to alert them.
Give them at least 4 feet of space.
Stay on the right side of your lane.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give them at least 4 feet of space.
questions.explanation: By law, you must leave at least 4 feet of space between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing them.
